author: 5kO0
content:
Surfaced by #22's wild-corpus rustc-compile test. One concrete case in the 420-lexicon wild slice:

  Source NSID:  com.bad-example.identity.resolveMiniDoc, com.bad-example.repo.getUriRecord
  Path written: target/wild-corpus-compile/src/generated/com/bad-example/...
  mod.rs decl:  pub mod bad_example;
  rustc:        E0583 file not found for module \`bad_example\`

The dash in the second NSID segment gets sanitized to \`_\` for the Rust identifier (correct) but the FILE PATH still uses the dash (\`bad-example/\`). Result: the parent mod.rs declares \`pub mod bad_example\` but Rust looks for \`bad_example.rs\` or \`bad_example/mod.rs\` — neither exists; only \`bad-example/\` does.

Per the atproto NSID spec (https://atproto.com/specs/nsid), segments are \`[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*\`, so dashes are legal. The bundled bsky/atproto/chat/tools corpus happens not to contain any dash-bearing NSIDs, which is why this is the first time it's surfaced.

Fix shape: in proto-blue-codegen, the path written to disk and the rust ident emitted in the declaring mod.rs must agree. Two reasonable approaches:
  A. Write both as the snake form (file path bad_example/, decl pub mod bad_example;) — loses fidelity to the original NSID in the directory layout but matches Rust convention.
  B. Write the path with the original segment and emit \`#[path = \"bad-example\"] pub mod bad_example;\` in the parent mod.rs — preserves original NSID in directory layout but adds a #[path] attribute.

Option A is simpler and matches what the rest of the codegen already does for the rust-ident side. Most likely it's a one-line fix in the path-construction code (probably to_snake_case-ing the segment when constructing the file path, mirroring what's already done for the mod-decl).

Search target: proto-blue-codegen/src/{main.rs,generator.rs} for the directory-path construction during mod-tree emission. Look for where NSID segments become path components — that's where the dash-preservation bug lives.
